description: Be-verb omission repair (audit commit ad3641395). Rule en-be-verb-omission inserts the missing copula in beginner '<pronoun> very <adjective>' sentences: I -> am, He/She/It -> is, You/We/They -> are, across the adjective set happy/sad/tired/busy (optionally followed by 'today'). Expectations encode the VERIFIED behaviour of correctWithTutorRules() on current main.
fp_risk_note: The copula-insertion must fire only when the copula is genuinely missing. The negative cases stress: (1) already-correct sentences that already contain 'am/is/are' before 'very' — inserting again would double the copula; (2) adjectives OUTSIDE the supported happy/sad/tired/busy set (e.g. 'cold') — the rule must abstain rather than guess; (3) non-copula uses of 'very' such as 'very much' where no adjective follows. KNOWN FALSE POSITIVE (documented in the MR, deliberately excluded from this golden because locking a buggy output as 'expected' would bless it): an inverted question 'Are you very happy?' currently fires and yields the double-copula 'Are you are very happy?'. A regression that broadens the pronoun/adjective match must re-check these.

positive.notes: First person -> 'am' (I very happy -> I am very happy).
Third person singular -> 'is' (He very tired -> He is very tired).

negative.notes: FP-stress (already correct): copula 'am' already present; rule must not double it.
FP-stress (adjective outside set): 'cold' is not in happy/sad/tired/busy, so the rule correctly abstains rather than guessing the copula.
FP-stress (non-copula 'very'): 'very much' is not '<pronoun> very <adjective>'; rule must not fire.
